page_title: KiwiDesk — Tiling that feels like it shipped with macOS

sources.entry: KiwiDesk - Tiling window manager that works out of the box with no config file, has a native Settings app, and updates itself from inside the app. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: KiwiDesk
summary.one_liner: KiwiDesk is a free tiling window manager for macOS that automatically arranges open windows as they are opened, configured through a built-in Settings app rather than a config file.
use_cases: automatically arrange open windows on a Mac
avoid manually resizing and dragging window edges
keep windows organized across macOS Spaces
quickly find and bring a lost window to the front
dim distractions while focusing on one window
keep a sticky window visible on every Space
summary.what_it_does: KiwiDesk places each window into a tiled position as it opens, sizing windows edge to edge so they stay usable as more are added. A hotkey (⌃⌥M) toggles the focused window to full screen and back to its tiled spot. Users can give apps their own shortcut keys, search windows by typing part of their name, and dim everything except the active window. It works alongside macOS Desktops/Spaces, restores windows to their Spaces after a restart, and can sync settings and profiles across Macs via iCloud Drive. Settings are in a SwiftUI app, and the page says it updates itself and can also be installed with Homebrew.
notable: Works out of the box with no config file; setup done in a native Settings app
Mouse support via Space Bar and App Bar overlays
Source code is public on GitHub
